# Status

Our Banking77 [@casanueva2020] intent classifier is written end to end in
PySpark (`spark/intent_classifier.py`). It ran unchanged on the 13,083-message
original, on a 905,828-row log from our own generator, and on 2M- and 10M-row
test logs, all under a 2 GB driver heap. New synthetic data is dropped in by
changing one path. Our full log has 44,464,114 rows but only 492,380 distinct
texts (EDA report), so it is the small-in-substance case: we wrote Spark now
so that growth needs no rewrite. Every run here used one 2-core machine
(Spark 3.5.3, `local[2]`); cluster runs are next (§5).

# The Spark job

Read the Hive-partitioned log (`date=`/`branch=` from the path) → route rows
with a label to training and rows without one to scoring, keeping planted
attack rows (`token_flooding`, `identity_fail_transfer`) out of training →
deduplicate by text and split 80/20 on a hash of the text → `RegexTokenizer`,
`NGram(2)`, `HashingTF` (2^15 buckets each), `IDF` → multinomial
`LogisticRegression` (L-BFGS, 100 iterations) → score the unlabeled rows,
writing `predictions/` (intent, confidence) partitioned by date and branch,
plus a weekly per-intent confidence table for drift monitoring. Only a 77×77
count table and a few aggregates ever reach the driver.

```bash
spark-submit --master spark://<master-private-ip>:7077 \
  --packages org.apache.hadoop:hadoop-aws:3.3.4 spark/intent_classifier.py \
  --log s3a://dsan6000-banking77-team/raw/ --intents scripts/intents.csv \
  --out s3a://dsan6000-banking77-team/model_v1/ --metrics metrics.json
```

# Wrestling with Spark

Memory and time depended on model width and partition layout, not on the
number of rows. The 2 GB cap was deliberate, so these problems would show up
before we pay for a cluster.

| Problem | Cause | Fix and effect |
|---|---|---|
| Out-of-memory error on the **13k-row** CSV | 2 × 2^18 features × 77 classes ≈ 40M dense coefficients, copied per L-BFGS task | `--num-features 32768`: fits in 2 GB |
| Out-of-memory error at 2M rows; 36 s per L-BFGS iteration | `groupBy("text")` left training data in 200 partitions, each returning a full 77 × 65,536 gradient | Repartition to 2 per core: 2.0–2.8 s per iteration |
| Scoring at ~600 msgs/s (≈55 min for 1.9M rows) | Unseen hash buckets have zero weight, so Spark stored the coefficients as a `SparseMatrix`, and every message walked all of it | Rebuild with `coefficientMatrix().toDense()`: 20,000 msgs in 38.9 s → 1.7 s, same predictions |
| Accuracy that cannot be trusted | Replayed messages are one sentence plus a prefix or suffix, so near-copies land on both sides of a split; `generate_log.py` also replays the official test split | Test on the official split with a train-only replay (below); fix the generator (§5) |

: Problems found and how we fixed them {#tbl-wrestle}

# Results

| Input | Rows | Training texts | Train (s) | Score + write (s) | Total (s) | Official test accuracy |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Banking77 CSV (train split) | 10,003 | 10,003 | 149 | – | 163 | 83.8% |
| Our generator's log, 90 days | 905,828 | 33,559 | 283 | 44 | 357 | n/a* |
| Train-only test log | 2,000,000 | 65,110 | 317 | 88 | 440 | 83.0% |
| Train-only test log | 10,000,000 | 189,739 | 492 | 384 | 935 | 83.3% |

: Same script, same 2 GB heap. *That log replays the test split, so official-test accuracy would leak. {#tbl-results}

Five times more rows (2M → 10M) took 2.1× as long in total. Scoring grew
4.4× and ran at 22,000–25,000 messages/s on two cores. Training grew only
1.6×, because it sees distinct reviewed texts, not rows. On held-out text,
more replayed rows did not help (83.0–83.3% vs 83.8%): the pipeline is not
the limit, the synthetic text is. Accuracy within each log is 98.8–99.98%,
which only measures near-duplicates.

One early fraud signal from our generator's log: the identity-check attack
rows got lower intent confidence than ordinary rows (0.77 vs 0.98), but the
token-flooding rows got 1.00. Confidence can be one feature of the risk
score, but it will not catch flooding on its own.

# Next steps

- Run the job on the 44.5M-row S3 log on the EC2 cluster (1 master + 4
  workers) at 1/10/100% of the data on 1, 2 and 4 workers, and record
  runtime, shuffle and partitions from the Spark UI. *Lanbin Fan, Ken Qin*
- Make `generate_log.py` replay only the training split and write a `base_id`
  per row, so the official 3,080-message test set stays unseen. *Ken Qin*
- Add Spark NLP sentence embeddings as a second model, and a fraud-risk score
  combining confidence, length and intent sequences. *Zizheng Wang*
- Feed `predictions/` and the drift table into the dashboard and the Quarto
  final report. *Lanbin Fan, Yixuan He*
